cards.explanation: The answer is that Paul will be cheered to learn how the Philippians are doing. He says he hopes to send Timothy soon, "…that I also may be cheered when I learn how you are doing." (Philippians 2:19) I know a little about wanting news from people you can't see, friends.

The word is "care." Paul says nobody else will "…genuinely care for your needs." (Philippians 2:20) Not care a little, not care when it's convenient. Genuinely. That's the kind of word you want said about you, friends.

The answer is False. Paul says, "For all the others look after their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ." (Philippians 2:21) The others look after their own interests, not Christ's. Timothy is the one who stands apart from that.

The answer is like a child with his father. Paul says Timothy "…as a child with his father he has served with me to advance the gospel." (Philippians 2:22) Paul and Timothy have a close bond. And the Philippians already know Timothy's proven worth, friends.

The answer is as soon as Paul sees what happens with him. Paul says, "So I hope to send him as soon as I see what happens with me." (Philippians 2:23) Paul is waiting to see how things go for him first. I wait on ovens all day, so I know a thing about waiting for the right moment, bakers.
The answer is True. Paul writes, "And I trust in the Lord that I myself will come soon." (Philippians 2:24) His trust is in the Lord, friends. That's a good place for it.

The answer is True. Paul calls Epaphroditus "…your messenger and minister to my needs." (Philippians 2:25) He's the Philippians' messenger, and he's also looking after Paul. That's a man with two jobs and one big heart, bakers.

The answer is that the Philippians heard he was ill. Paul says Epaphroditus "…has been longing for all of you and is distressed because you heard he was ill." (Philippians 2:26) He's the one who was ill, and he's distressed that they heard about it. I think that's a good heart on him, friends.

The answer is False. Paul says, "…God had mercy on him, and not only on him but also on me, to spare me sorrow upon sorrow." (Philippians 2:27) Epaphroditus got mercy, and so did Paul. The mercy didn't stop at one man, friends.

The word is "anxious." Paul says he's eager to send Epaphroditus "…so that when you see him again you may rejoice, and I may be less anxious." (Philippians 2:28) The Philippians may rejoice, and Paul may be less anxious. I think everybody sleeps better once a friend is home, bakers.

The answer is for the work of Christ. Paul says Epaphroditus "…nearly died for the work of Christ…" (Philippians 2:30) That's why he tells the Philippians to welcome him with great joy and honor men like him. It's a lot to give for the work of Christ, friends.
